newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo tourism down 7.0 pct in Jan-Oct - statistics.
newsitem.headline: Yugo tourism down 7.0 pct in Jan-Oct - statistics.

text.p: Around 2.5 million tourists registered in Yugoslavia from January to October this year, or seven percent less than in the same period in 1995, the Federal Statistics Office said Friday.
Yugoslavs accounted for 2.28 million of the total, a drop of 10 percent from the same period last year. Some 139,000 foreigners visited the country, an increase of 69 percent.
The greatest number of foreign tourists, 16,812, came from the Russian Federaton, followed by 14,435 from Italy, 11,287 from Greece, 10,405 from Bulgaria and 10,207 from Germany.
The number of vistiors from other republics of the former Yugoslavia -- Bosnia, Croatia, Macedonia and Slovenia -- rose 9.4 percent from a year earlier to 120,794.
According to National Bank of Yugoslavia data, hard currency income from tourism in the January-September period was $31.5 million, down 6.5 percent on the same period in 1995.
